production.note: US model years. US cars are sold as 2008 models (TTAC, SCM and Ulrich all describe the '2008 Alfa Romeo 8C Competizione'). SCM gives coupe production as "2007–09"; no opened page confirms a 2009 US model year, so endYear 2009 is the end of production. The 8C Spider is a separate car.

body.note: "Only 500 Alfa 8C Competizione coupes will be built" (egm-8c-review); "90 for the U.S. market" (SCM).

drivetrain.note: Front-engined with a rear transaxle; inferred from the descriptions

transmission.note: "The transmission, which had six speeds, was an automated manual". Ulrich: "six-speed, Formula One-style automated manual transmission". SCM calls it a "twin-clutch transaxle", which the other sources contradict.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (named-author articles; no manufacturer page opened). Alfa Romeo's 450 CV/PS rating converted: 450 x 0.98632 = 444 hp. Quote (TTAC, Corey Lewis): "Power on offer was a considerable 444 horses and 354 lb-ft of torque." SCM (Jeff Zurschmeide): "444 horsepower and 354 lb-ft of torque". Evo's spec panel: "450bhp @ 7000rpm"; Lawrence Ulrich (US launch review): "a new, 4.7-liter V8 with 450 horsepower"; these print the metric figure. No US-specific rating from Alfa Romeo/Maserati North America was found.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (one named-author article plus an enthusiast site). Quote (TTAC): "Lighter construction methods kept weight down to 3,494 pounds." Supercar Nostalgia (supercarnostalgia-8c): "The 8C Competizione weighed 1585kg" (= 3,494 lb). SCM calls it the curb weight: "curb weight of the 8C about a bag of doughnuts under 3,500 pounds". Evo's text also gives 1585kg ("helping keep the 8C's weight down to 1585kg", evo-8c, if listed) without a label.

sources.title: Rare Rides: A 2008 Alfa Romeo 8C Competizione, Exquisitely Italian
Review: 2008 Alfa Romeo 8C Competizione test drive

reviewNotes: 1) Weight 1,585 kg / 3,494 lb is called a curb weight only by Sports Car Market; no Alfa Romeo figure was opened. 2) Power: 450 CV converted to 444 hp; whether Alfa/Maserati North America published a US hp figure (Ulrich says '450 horsepower') is unconfirmed. 3) US model years beyond 2008 are unconfirmed (endYear 2009 is SCM's end of production).
provisionalNote: Power (444 hp from 450 CV) rests on TTAC and Sports Car Market (agreeing), with Evo's panel and Ulrich printing 450; weight (3,494 lb) rests on TTAC and Supercar Nostalgia (1,585 kg), basis unstated. An Alfa Romeo/Maserati press kit or a major magazine (Car and Driver, Road & Track, MotorTrend, Evo, Autocar) spec panel with a labelled weight would replace both.
